opportunities.description: Office support at the Fremont location. Most direct-service roles are adults-only, but there are youth placements.
opportunities.title: Youth office volunteer

opportunities.description: Shelving, tidying, cleaning materials and helping run library programs. Posted for high school students only. Shifts run 4pm to 6pm, two hours at a time, up to twice a week and ten hours a quarter. Training on your first day. Sign up through Alameda County Library's Better Impact page.
opportunities.title: Volunteer shelving at Castro Valley Library

opportunities.description: Planting and maintaining trees around Fremont. Event-based, signup through their site. Age policy is not posted — ask when you sign up.
opportunities.title: Tree planting and care days

opportunities.description: Centro asks for youth volunteers at its community thrift store on H Street and at the Wednesday morning produce hand-out. Groceries go out the last Thursday of each month. No age floor is posted — call 510-489-4100.
opportunities.title: Thrift shop and Wednesday produce distribution

opportunities.description: Teens support library programs and events — children's craft programs, the summer learning registration table, community outreach — and serve as library advisors. Members earn community service hours. Each branch signs up separately.
opportunities.title: Teens Reach library volunteer

opportunities.description: LOV is the Tri-City volunteer clearinghouse for Fremont, Newark and Union City. Teen volunteers help lead activities and assist staff at the summer recreation camps for elementary-age kids, which is real leadership experience. Under 18 needs parental consent. Office is open weekdays 8am to 5pm.
opportunities.title: Teen summer program leader

opportunities.description: Roughly one two-hour shift a week. Shelving, program setup and help at events. Some assignments need a background check.
opportunities.title: Teen library volunteer

opportunities.description: Processing requests, sorting food and clothing and stocking shelves at the Ash Street center, plus seasonal toy collection and the children's Christmas party. No age policy is posted — call (510) 794-3437 or email violablythectr@gmail.com to ask.
opportunities.title: Sorting food and clothing at the center

opportunities.description: Onsite shifts are for adult volunteers, but students can still help from home: foster a pet with a parent or guardian, or sew no-sew fleece blankets for shelter animals, which earns half an hour of credit each. Email volunteer@hssv.org for a letter verifying your hours.
opportunities.title: Remote student volunteering for shelter animals

opportunities.description: The city lists special event help, park maintenance, Ruggieri Center senior support and art teaching. Nothing about age appears online — call Community & Recreation Services at 510-471-3232 and ask which roles take students.
opportunities.title: Recreation and special event volunteer

opportunities.description: R.A.V.E.N. places community volunteers with the police department, explicitly including high school students weighing a career in law enforcement. Ask the community engagement manager at 510-578-4929 about current openings.
opportunities.title: Police department community volunteer (R.A.V.E.N.)

opportunities.description: Park cleanup and beautification events, usually 8:45am to noon with supplies provided, posted on the city's volunteer calendar. The city verifies community service hours. No age floor is published — email ParkVolunteer@sanjoseca.gov to ask.
opportunities.org: City of San José Parks, Recreation & Neighborhood Services
opportunities.title: One-day park volunteer events

opportunities.description: The Tri-Valley's hot meal program. Volunteers prep and serve lunches at the Pleasanton Senior Center, with other sites at the Dublin Senior Center and in Livermore. The floor is 16 even with a guardian, and weekend shifts are restricted to grown-ups, so students volunteer on weekdays. volunteerservices@openheartkitchen.org.
opportunities.title: Meal service at the senior center

opportunities.description: A week-long summer session for high school students weighing a career in criminal justice. Runs as a single cohort rather than ongoing shifts. Email Catalina.Medeles@dublin.ca.gov about the next one.
opportunities.title: Law Enforcement Youth Academy

opportunities.description: Year-round placements for students 16 and up in good academic standing, including the gift shop and patient-facing roles. Requires an application and a time commitment.
opportunities.title: Hospital volunteer program

opportunities.description: Weeding, mulching and raking in the rose, shade and succulent gardens. Tools and training provided; 9am to noon, stay for as much as you want. Wear closed-toe shoes and bring water.
opportunities.title: Historic garden upkeep, first Saturday of the month

opportunities.description: Sorting and packing produce and dry goods at two San Jose warehouses. The floor is 12, but 12-to-15s need one adult per five youths, so in practice you can only sign up alone at 16. They don't sign third-party hour forms — print a timecard each shift and your history stays on your account.
opportunities.title: Food sorting at the Curtner and Cypress centers

opportunities.description: One of the largest food distributors in Alameda County. During school breaks, high-school-age volunteers can drop in on a first-come basis to help with distribution and the thrift store.
opportunities.title: Food distribution helper

opportunities.description: Help elementary students with homework at the Kennedy Youth Center on Decoto Road. The center runs drop-in Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday afternoons and opens earlier on Wednesday. No age floor is posted — call 510.675.5329.
opportunities.title: Elementary homework assistant at Kennedy Youth Center

opportunities.description: The city takes individual and group volunteers for community programs and projects, including the Jr. Golden State basketball league. Read the Volunteer Program Guide first, then apply through the city's job portal. No age floor is posted — email recreation@dublin.ca.gov.
opportunities.org: City of Dublin Parks & Community Services
opportunities.title: Community programs and projects volunteer

opportunities.description: LOV has run a free community Thanksgiving dinner for close to four decades, alongside holiday food and toy drives and an Adopt-A-Family program. Volunteers under 18 need parental consent; no age floor is posted for the dinner itself. Call (510) 793-5683.
opportunities.title: Community Thanksgiving dinner and holiday drives

opportunities.description: Event-based sessions at the Fremont Main Library supporting children with special needs. They recruit high-school volunteers for each session.
opportunities.title: Community Circle for children with special needs

opportunities.description: Annual all-ages cleanup run through the city. Also worth checking their Adopt-A-Drain program for something ongoing.
opportunities.title: Coastal Cleanup Day

opportunities.description: Filing, mailing prep and light data entry, about 1.5 to 3 hours a week between Monday and Thursday, typically 3:30 to 5pm. Runs year round.
opportunities.title: Clerical support for the library foundation

opportunities.description: Work alongside librarians in the children's section — cleaning books, prepping crafts and helping where needed. Open to grades 7 through 12, in one-hour shifts you schedule yourself. Applications open during the school year; ask hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov.
opportunities.title: Children's room helper

opportunities.description: Cat care, dog care and treatment room support at the Nevada Street adoption center. Animal care starts at 16; AniMeals and customer service are older. They want one set weekly shift and roughly six months, and they don't take drop-ins.
opportunities.title: Cat, dog and treatment room care

opportunities.description: Animal care, docent work, gardening and summer wildlife camp counseling at the rec district's nature center. Open from 13 up, but they ask for a real commitment: one 2-to-4-hour shift a week for a year, plus a TB test. nature@haywardrec.org.
opportunities.title: Animal care and docent volunteer

opportunities.description: Help elementary students with homework and STEAM activities, supervise outdoor time and assist teachers. Training provided and they explicitly welcome students working on service hours.
opportunities.title: Afterschool program tutor
